subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Section 230 Debate
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Section 230 Debate.

hook.text: A 1996 law shields social media from lawsuits over what users post. It's called the internet's most important law.

buildup.text: Section 230 says platforms are not publishers. They can host user content without being liable for it.

discovery.text: Without Section 230, platforms would face lawsuits for every harmful post — making social media impossible.

twist.text: Critics say platforms use 230 as a shield while profiting from harmful content they could moderate better.

climax.text: Section 230 enabled the modern internet. Reforming it could reshape online speech for everyone.

punchline.text: One law. The internet depends on it.

quiz.question: What does Section 230 protect platforms from?
options: Legal liability for content posted by their users
